version.changelog: Replaced imgbb with Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs (1 min expiry) for local image uploads. Added boto3 dependency. No longer requires imgbb API key.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions broadly match its stated purpose (RunPod media generation), but there are inconsistent metadata declarations and it requests high‑privilege Cloudflare R2 credentials (and will read your local ~/.openclaw/secrets.json), which is disproportionate enough to warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The scripts implement image/video generation, editing, and endpoint discovery exactly as the name/description promise. However the packaged metadata is inconsistent: the top-level registry summary claimed no required binaries/env, while _meta.json and the scripts require the 'uv' runner and RunPod + Cloudflare R2 secrets. The need for R2 credentials is plausible (the skill uploads local files to R2 before calling RunPod) but is a high-privilege requirement that should be justified to users.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the Python scripts limit actions to resolving/uploading local files, calling RunPod endpoints, polling job status, and saving results under ~/.openclaw/workspace/runpod-media. There are a few stale/inconsistent docs lines (mentions imgbb in edit section despite R2 being used) and the discover_endpoints 'add' mode will write to the local endpoints.json in the skill folder. No instructions attempt to read arbitrary system files beyond ~/.openclaw/secrets.json.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no network download/extract install step (low install risk). The package includes runnable scripts and expects Python dependencies (requests, boto3) and the 'uv' runner; but no install spec is provided, so runtime may fail if those aren't present. That lack of an install prescription is an operational gap but not itself malicious.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a RunPod API key (reasonable) and Cloudflare R2 credentials (accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, endpoint, bucket). R2 keys are powerful — they grant access to object storage — and are stored/read from ~/.openclaw/secrets.json by the scripts. The code reads that secrets.json file directly (and in one path loads the R2 sub-dictionary), which could expose other secrets if the file is broader than expected. Requiring full R2 keys is proportionate only if you need local-file uploads; if you will only pass URLs, you can avoid giving R2 rights.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-on and does not request special platform privileges. It writes output files to ~/.openclaw/workspace/runpod-media and may modify its own endpoints.json when using discover_endpoints add — both are limited to the skill directory and workspace. It does not modify other skills or global agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill generally does what it says: it uploads local images to Cloudflare R2 (via credentials in ~/.openclaw/secrets.json), calls RunPod endpoints, and saves media in your OpenClaw workspace. Before installing: 1) Verify the metadata mismatch — ensure the skill owner/slug is trustworthy (the package claims different requirements in places). 2) Prefer supplying only a RunPod API key if you won't upload local files; avoid giving long-lived R2 keys unless necessary. If you must provide R2 credentials, create a minimized API token scoped only to a single bucket and with tight expiration/rotation. 3) Ensure 'uv' and Python deps (requests, boto3) are available or sandbox the skill to prevent unexpected network access. 4) Be aware discover_endpoints add will write to endpoints.json and probes endpoints using your RunPod key (network activity is expected). If you want higher assurance, inspect or run the scripts in a restricted environment (or request the skill author to remove the need to read entire secrets.json and to document required minimal permissions).
